claims.text: A predictive approach using mass-variance and force-constant-fluctuation metrics can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The disorder-metric approach will outperform conventional methods based on average crystallographic parameters.
Fe20Co20Cr20Mn20Ni20 is an equiatomic, chemically disordered high-entropy alloy with a simple crystalline lattice.
Local-configuration disorder metrics can be used to estimate phonon-scattering rates and thermal conductivity.
There are temperature regimes in which lattice vibrations dominate transport and electron-phonon interactions are weak.
The proposed approach applies when inherent chemical disorder is the primary influence on phonon lifetimes.
Strong chemical disorder in HEAs produces significant atomic-mass fluctuations.
Strong chemical disorder in HEAs produces significant interatomic force-constant fluctuations.
Mass and force-constant fluctuations enhance phonon scattering and reduce phonon lifetimes.
Disorder-induced reductions in phonon lifetime reduce effective thermal conductivity.
Explicitly modeling disorder captures HEA phonon dynamics better than conventional models.
The model will reduce prediction error by approximately 20–30% relative to standard averaging techniques.
Experimental measurements will agree with the model predictions within defined uncertainty bounds.
Current average-property methods neglect local disorder effects.
Neglecting local disorder causes current methods to overestimate phonon lifetimes and thermal conductivity.
HEAs are crystalline random alloys containing four or more elements in a simple unit cell.
The approach is primarily applicable to HEAs and other disordered crystals whose phonon dynamics are governed by chemical randomness.
The approach may have limited utility when electron-phonon interactions or other scattering mechanisms dominate.
Microstructural imperfections, secondary phases, processing history, and electronic thermal transport can confound isolation of chemical-disorder effects.
Inelastic neutron and X-ray scattering can be used to investigate the lattice and phonon dynamics of Fe20Co20Cr20Mn20Ni20.
